I'm curious. What do you take pride in? Is it really only things that can be traced to conscious decisions of yours? For most people the answer is no, but I suppose it might be yes for you.

Being born in a particular country, or with good parents (good defined however you want, it's subjective), or with a well formed genetically predisposed athletic body, or with a high IQ or anything else is not something you choose. Nonetheless, it doesn't mean you may not have pride that you are smart or can run fast or even that your school football team/mathletes/band won districts even if you are not a member of that activity. It is pretty normal human behavior to take pride in the successes for things you didn't plan for or of groups to which you belong. It helps incentivize people to exertthemselves and helps build cohesive societies. I personally think it is a good things up to and including patriotism for one's nation-state.

Any source of pride can be used to ill purpose. That even includes things your are proud of that are wholly attributable to your decisions and efforts. So I do not see patriotism as a negative, but it can have negative consequences. There is a reason pride is one of the seven deadly sins after all.

Being proud of your country might not make sense but being proud of its culture, society and history isn't so much. The society and culture you're brought up in can have a big effect on you personally so it makes sense to feel a sense of pride in something like that, so that you can defend it with a greater sense of conviction. Personally, I don't think patriotism makes much sense - in a lot of ways it's just a feeling that has been abused by governments so many times in order to coerce or guilt the population into following or at least not objecting to concerns they may have. But it may make sense to some.

It's not hurting anyone, and it's in our nature to feel like we belong in a group.
